name: Huron University College
summary: The collegiate complex combines stepped academic roofs, a tilted solar array, west annex, Tudor timber, glazed gabled entry, and basement-well edges around the limestone chapel and battlemented bell tower.

evidence.note: Courtyard entrance framed by brick and pale horizontal bands, projecting gabled hood and white double-hung windows.
Stepped brick bay and projecting sills on a residence elevation.
The chapel has tall leaded pointed windows and exposed pitched timber roof.
Distant view across the lawn shows the pitched chapel and small spire against the sky.
Red brick residence with pitched roof, dormers and pale-framed rectangular windows behind the dining hall.

Grey ridges turn at right angles on the three residence wings. Repeated dormers, a chapel projection toward Western Road and flat rectangular roofs enclosing two sides of the paved court are distinct.
Ground-relative P50 10.56 m, P90 13.65 m and maximum 20.22 m.

Wall colour sampled with PIL. Photo https://huronu.ca/wp-content/uploads/oneil-ridley-01-1024x683.jpg at normalized pixel (0.351, 0.654). Roof tone sampled from the 2025 orthophoto. Dimensions and bay counts on obscured elevations are estimates.
Individual dormer centres follow the three long ridges in the 2025 orthophoto. The red entrance fascia is visible in the Huron residence gallery.
Huron's 2026 viewbook page 34 shows a substantial limestone bell tower with a corner copper spire, timber-framed dormers, and a solar array behind the chapel.
Regional lidar around (-84,242) measures 17–18 m over the square shaft with a local sample close to 20 m at the corner, and the thin spire tip height is estimated from the photograph.
